findings.summary: EVERY_SPEC_FILES omits .joycraft/references/worktrees.md, which every implementer and reviewer reads on every spec: dispatch-preflight.mjs:400 lists it in both roles' referencePaths without a condition, :468 makes it packet readFirst, and :470 says "Read the listed files first." The comment at tests/payload-guard.test.ts:24-26 states the opposite. The spec's parenthetical names five references and the code matches that literal list, but the criterion and the coordinator interpretation define every-spec as "the references they always read per spec" / "text an agent reads while working a spec", which worktrees.md is. Fix: add worktrees.md with its reason, recompute the constants (base on-demand 17,663: caps 12,256 and 19,663; now 12,150 and 17,569, same 106 / 2,094 spare), correct the comment, and add worktrees.md to the spec's list. The cap still holds after the fix, so no text was moved to dodge the cap today; the error widens what may grow later.
findings.assumption: The parenthetical list is the decomposer's enumeration of the definition, not a closed definition; the reading closest to the brief ("text read on every spec stays flat") wins.

findings.summary: The cap-raise option text says every-spec is "skills, agents, the references they always read"; the coordinator interpretation (spec 98ea7bd) puts the session-end, entry, context, cleanup, retro and ui-slice skills on-demand. Under the original spec grouping the spare is the same 106 words, so this does not dodge today's cap, but about 10,300 words (occasional skills plus conditional references) now share the +2,000 growth budget. Session-end runs once per queue unattended. Owner may want to confirm the narrowing.
findings.assumption: The decision context "text read on every spec stays flat" governs over the shorthand "skills".

findings.summary: The spec-mandated cut of joycraft-testing:34-37 was not a full duplicate: "Do not commit tests of one-off run state" and "or conflicts with a later owner decision" now appear nowhere in the payload (probe git grep: none). implement:59 and joycraft-implementer.md:26 keep the rest. Spec 22 plans to cut implement:59 too; it should keep these clauses somewhere.

The 200-word fixture fails the every-spec cap only while spare is under 200 (106 now). Later cuts (spec 22 and others) can raise spare past 200 and make this test fail with no regression. Adding (EVERY_SPEC_CAP - everySpec + 1) words, or asserting at least that, keeps the check stable.
The allowlist entry for WorktreeCreate in setup.md no longer matches any line after the cut; it can be removed.
